 Julian Champagnie is building a strong case to take Devin Vassell’s starting spot 
 He'd make the Spurs starting five better. By Cal Durrett | Nov 18, 2026, 7:00 AM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Julian Champagnie | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect San Antonio Spurs forward Julian Champagnie is making a strong case for a starting spot , especially given their recent shooting struggles. Champagnie has plenty of experience starting on the Spurs, having previously started 162 games with the team. 
--> San Antonio Spurs forward Julian Champagnie is making a strong case for a starting spot , especially given their recent shooting struggles. Champagnie has plenty of experience starting on the Spurs, having previously started 162 games with the team. 
 That experience would make him a seamless fit in the starting five, and he played well when filling in for Vassell. When starting, he averaged 11.5 points while shooting 40% from three on 7.5 3-point attempts per game this season. 
--> That experience would make him a seamless fit in the starting five, and he played well when filling in for Vassell. When starting, he averaged 11.5 points while shooting 40% from three on 7.5 3-point attempts per game this season. 
 More importantly, the Spurs' offense was rolling, with them averaging 123.5 points in those starts. Still, Vassell is arguably the team's best all-around shooter, while Champagnie is likely the Spurs' best 3-point shooter. 
--> More importantly, the Spurs' offense was rolling, with them averaging 123.5 points in those starts. Still, Vassell is arguably the team's best all-around shooter, while Champagnie is likely the Spurs' best 3-point shooter. 
 He's been molten hot from outside, drilling 42.1% of his threes per game. Champagnie has given the Spurs a much-needed knockdown shooter that teams don't dare leave open. He also gives the starting five more size, with him being four inches taller than Vassell and a far superior rebounder. 
--> He's been molten hot from outside, drilling 42.1% of his threes per game. Champagnie has given the Spurs a much-needed knockdown shooter that teams don't dare leave open. He also gives the starting five more size, with him being four inches taller than Vassell and a far superior rebounder. 
 Julian Champagnie should replace Devin Vassell in the starting five
--> Julian Champagnie should replace Devin Vassell in the starting five
 Between Champagnie and Vassell, Vassell is the better defender, though Champagnie is more versatile on that end of the floor. The Spurs really can't go wrong with either, though starting Champagnie comes with a couple of additional benefits. 
--> Between Champagnie and Vassell, Vassell is the better defender, though Champagnie is more versatile on that end of the floor. The Spurs really can't go wrong with either, though starting Champagnie comes with a couple of additional benefits. 
 As good as Vassell is as a shooter, he hasn't been nearly as effective this season. In fact, he's shooting nearly 12% worse from three this season compared to Champagnie, connecting on just 31.5% from outside.
--> As good as Vassell is as a shooter, he hasn't been nearly as effective this season. In fact, he's shooting nearly 12% worse from three this season compared to Champagnie, connecting on just 31.5% from outside.
 San Antonio is also starting four guards, which has resulted in them having four forwards coming off the bench. Starting Champagnie would help to alleviate that issue by moving Vassell to the second unit, where his scoring could shine. 
--> San Antonio is also starting four guards, which has resulted in them having four forwards coming off the bench. Starting Champagnie would help to alleviate that issue by moving Vassell to the second unit, where his scoring could shine. 
 It would also free up Tobias Harris to potentially play a larger role once he makes his Spurs debut. 
--> It would also free up Tobias Harris to potentially play a larger role once he makes his Spurs debut. 
 Devin Vassell could solve the Spurs' second-unit concerns
--> Devin Vassell could solve the Spurs' second-unit concerns
 Carter Bryant would have an easier path to minutes with him not having to compete with Champagnie for minutes off the bench. Clearing up that potential logjam forward could make the Spurs all the more dangerous. 
--> Carter Bryant would have an easier path to minutes with him not having to compete with Champagnie for minutes off the bench. Clearing up that potential logjam forward could make the Spurs all the more dangerous. 
 San Antonio already struggles when Wembanyama is on the bench, so moving Vassell, who's a well-wounded scorer, to the second unit could help ease those concerns.
--> San Antonio already struggles when Wembanyama is on the bench, so moving Vassell, who's a well-wounded scorer, to the second unit could help ease those concerns.
 After all, he can be a volatile scorer who can get hot in a hurry, which actually lends itself to coming off the bench. Pair him with a healthy Harris, Kornet, Keldon Johnson, and one of De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, or Dylan Harper, and the second unit should hold their own offensively.
--> After all, he can be a volatile scorer who can get hot in a hurry, which actually lends itself to coming off the bench. Pair him with a healthy Harris, Kornet, Keldon Johnson, and one of De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, or Dylan Harper, and the second unit should hold their own offensively.
 Overall, Champagnie has played well this season and could give San Antonio starting lineup a different look. As for Vassell, when Harris returns, the Spurs could shake up the starting five, and he might be asked to come off the bench, where he could potentially thrive.
